# Citation

Baumdicker, F., et al. (2022). *Efficient ancestry and mutation simulation with msprime 1.0*. PLoS Computational Biology. DOI: 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1004842. Source: [https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9176297/](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9176297/).

# One-Sentence Summary

Presents msprime 1.0 for efficient ancestry and mutation simulation using tree-sequence approaches.

# Scope for simitall

Use as a potential future engine for large neutral or demographic simulations and as a source of founder haplotypes. It is complementary to designed-cross breeding simulations.

# Agent-Safe Takeaways

- Coalescent simulation can generate large ancestry datasets efficiently.
- Tree sequences compactly represent correlated genealogical histories.
- Demographic assumptions must be explicit before treating a simulated panel as realistic.

# Inputs to Specify

- Sample configuration
- Demographic model
- Recombination and mutation rates

# Expected Outputs

- Ancestry tree sequences
- Mutated genotype data
- Population-genetic summaries

# Limitations and Guardrails

- Coalescent panels do not automatically reflect a real breeding pedigree or selected population.
- Use real haplotype panels when empirical LD and allele spectra matter.

# Questions This Record Can Ground

- When should a synthetic founder panel use a coalescent engine?
- What differs between ancestry simulation and a designed mating scheme?
